text:
# Persistence and Storage Layout

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-047 |
| Owner | Felix Wagner |
| Last updated | 2026-07-09 |

All persistent connectivity data is stored in the encrypted partition **`/persist/bt/`** (dm-crypt, key bound to the HU4 hardware).

```
/persist/bt/
  pairing/            COMP-003 records (protobuf), one file per device
  phonebook/          COMP-007 SQLite DBs, one per device (<deviceIdHash>.db)
  diag/               COMP-005 ring buffer file
  settings.json       Connectivity settings (per vehicle)
  stack/              Nimbus stack internal files (do not edit)
```

## Rules

- Only the owning component writes to its folder.
- Writes are atomic (temp file + rename) for pairing and settings.
- The SQLite DBs use WAL mode.
- The budget for the whole partition is 64 MB (REQ-029).

## Backup

There is no backup of `/persist/bt/`. After a head unit replacement in the workshop, phones must be paired again.

## Factory reset

`FactoryReset()` of COMP-003 removes `pairing/`, `phonebook/` and `settings.json`, and clears the ring buffer in `diag/`.
title: Persistence and Storage Layout

text:
# Error Handling and Error Codes

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-048 |
| Owner | Radu Ionescu |
| Last updated | 2026-08-12 |

## PCON result codes

| Code | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | OK | Success |
| 1 | E_TRANSIENT | Transient communication error – eligible for retry (REQ-004) |
| 2 | E_AUTH | Authentication failed (key missing or rejected) |
| 3 | E_NOT_REACHABLE | Page timeout after retry |
| 4 | E_PROFILE | Profile could not be restored |
| 5 | E_INTERNAL | Internal error in PCON or stack |
| 6 | E_CANCELLED | Attempt cancelled (ignition off, low voltage) |

## Mapping of HCI errors

| HCI error | Name | PCON code | Transient? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x04 | Page timeout | E_TRANSIENT | Yes |
| 0x08 | Connection timeout | E_TRANSIENT | Yes |
| 0x22 | LMP response timeout | E_TRANSIENT | Yes |
| 0x05 | Authentication failure | E_AUTH | No |
| 0x06 | PIN or key missing | E_AUTH | No |
| 0x0D–0x0F | Connection rejected (resources/security/address) | E_INTERNAL | No |

## Errors observed but not yet classified

The following HCI errors have been seen in HiL and vehicle traces during connection setup but are not yet mapped:

- 0x0B – ACL connection already exists
- 0x0C – Command disallowed

Until they are classified, COMP-009 maps them to E_INTERNAL.

## Logging

Every error is logged with the HCI code and the PCON code (PC-049).

text:
# Logging Conventions and Trace Format

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-049 |
| Owner | Elena Rusu |
| Last updated | 2026-08-25 |

## Trace line format

```
<ISO-8601 timestamp> <LEVEL> <component> <attemptId> <message>
```

Example:

```
2026-07-21T08:45:03.120 INFO COMP-001 - Vehicle ignition event received.
2026-07-21T08:45:12.004 WARN COMP-009 a7f3 Reconnection request remained in the connection queue for 8.9 seconds.
2026-07-21T08:45:21.007 ERROR COMP-002 a7f3 Phone reconnected in 18.0 seconds and exceeded the 10-second limit.
```

## Levels

| Level | Use |
|---|---|
| ERROR | Requirement violated or function failed |
| WARN | Unexpected but recovered situation |
| INFO | State changes, start/end of attempts |
| DEBUG | Detailed protocol information |

Development and HiL builds log at DEBUG level.

## Trace repository

Traces of HiL and vehicle executions are uploaded to the TraceRepository and linked to the execution ID (TRACE-xxx).

## Diagnostic event buffer

In addition to text traces, COMP-005 keeps a ring buffer of the last **1000** diagnostic events which survives power cycles.

## Personal data in traces

Traces currently contain the device name reported by the phone (often the owner's first name) and the BD_ADDR. Whether device names and addresses must be pseudonymized in traces is an **open point** with the Cybersecurity team.
title: Logging Conventions and Trace Format

text:
# Threading and Timing Model

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-050 |
| Owner | Andrei Popescu |
| Last updated | 2026-07-28 |

## Processes

Each component runs in its own process, except COMP-002 and COMP-006, which share the process `pcon-connmgr`.

| Process | Components | Scheduling |
|---|---|---|
| pcon-connmgr | COMP-002, COMP-006 | SCHED_OTHER, nice −5 |
| pcon-stack | COMP-009 + Nimbus stack | SCHED_FIFO, prio 20 |
| pcon-profiles | COMP-004 | SCHED_OTHER |
| pcon-pbap | COMP-007 | SCHED_OTHER, nice 5 |
| pcon-diag | COMP-005 | SCHED_OTHER, nice 5 |
| pcon-store | COMP-003 | SCHED_OTHER |
| pcon-vehicle | COMP-001, COMP-010 | SCHED_OTHER |
| pcon-hmi | COMP-008 | SCHED_OTHER |

## Event loop

Every process uses a single-threaded event loop (libuv). Blocking operations (file I/O, HSM calls) are executed in a worker pool of 2 threads per process.

## Timers

- All timers use the monotonic clock.
- Timestamps in diagnostic events use the system clock (UTC), synchronized by the platform; before time synchronization, timestamps are relative to boot.

## Timing budget at startup

| Phase | Budget |
|---|---|
| Connectivity components started | ≤ 1.5 s (REQ-030) |
| BT_READY | ≤ 3 s after component start (assumption A2) |
| Reconnection | ≤ 10 s after BT_READY (REQ-002) |
title: Threading and Timing Model

text:
# ADR-001 – Single Retry with Fixed Delay

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-051 |
| Status | **Accepted** (2026-06-19) |
| Deciders | Tobias Kern, Andrei Popescu, Radu Ionescu, Mara Lindqvist |

## Context

REQ-004 requires a retry when the first reconnection attempt fails because of a transient communication error. The number of retries and the delay were not fixed by the requirement. The 10-second limit of REQ-002 limits how much time can be spent on retries: a page timeout alone takes 5.12 s.

## Options

1. **Single retry with a fixed delay.**
2. Up to three retries with exponential backoff (1 s, 2 s, 4 s).
3. Continuous retries until the give-up timer expires.

## Decision

Option 1: **exactly one retry**, after a fixed delay of **2 seconds**.

## Rationale

- With a page timeout of 5.12 s, a second retry can never finish within 10 s.
- The 2-second delay gives the phone time to finish its own Bluetooth activities (e.g. a connection to a headset that is being released) and reduces the chance that the retry fails for the same reason.
- Exponential backoff adds complexity without benefit within the 10-second window.
- Continuous retries would block the radio for the secondary phone.

## Consequences

- REQ-004 is interpreted as "one retry" (PC-015).
- Phones that are not reachable within the first attempt plus one retry are handled by the give-up logic (PC-042).
- The test TEST-004 verifies exactly one retry.
title: ADR-001 – Single Retry with Fixed Delay

text:
# ADR-002 – Most-Recently-Used Priority for Multiple Phones

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-052 |
| Status | **Accepted** (2026-06-26) |
| Deciders | Tobias Kern, Mara Lindqvist, Radu Ionescu, Jonas Weber |

## Context

With REQ-008 the system supports up to two connected phones. When several paired phones are in range after ignition, the system must decide which phone becomes the primary phone (HFP + A2DP + PBAP) and which one becomes secondary (HFP only).

## Options

1. **Most-Recently-Used (MRU):** the phone with the latest successful connection is primary.
2. **Pairing order:** the first paired phone is primary.
3. **Signal strength:** the phone with the strongest RSSI is primary.
4. **Driver identification:** use the key fob / user profile to select the phone.

## Decision

Option 1: **MRU** based on the timestamp of the last successful connection stored in COMP-003. Maximum **two** phones are connected simultaneously.

## Rationale

- MRU matches the behavior of HU3 and of most competitor systems.
- Signal strength is unreliable: a passenger's phone near the head unit could win.
- Driver identification depends on the user-profile feature of the HMI Platform, which is not stable for R1.

## Consequences

- The driver can change the primary phone manually; the change updates the MRU order.
- COMP-006 implements the sorting (PC-037).

## Open point: favourite phone

Product Management (Mara Lindqvist) asked for a "favourite phone" setting: the driver marks one phone as favourite, and this phone shall always become primary when it is in range. It is **not decided** whether a favourite overrides MRU in all cases, only when both phones are in range, or whether the feature is postponed. To be discussed with the HMI Platform team.
title: ADR-002 – Most-Recently-Used Priority for Multiple Phones

text:
# ADR-003 – Encrypted Link-Key Storage with HSM Key Wrapping

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-053 |
| Status | **Accepted** (2026-07-08) |
| Deciders | Karim Haddad, Tobias Kern, Felix Wagner |

## Context

Bluetooth link keys allow impersonation of a paired phone if they are extracted from the vehicle. The TARA (PC-095) rated link-key extraction from flash as a relevant threat. REQ-022 requires encrypted storage.

## Options

1. Rely on the encrypted partition `/persist/bt/` only.
2. **Wrap each link key with a key held in the HSM** and store only the wrapped key.
3. Store link keys inside the HSM secure storage.

## Decision

Option 2. Each link key is wrapped with **AES-256-GCM** using a device-unique wrapping key that never leaves the HSM. The wrapped key is stored by COMP-003; unwrapping happens at connection time and the plain key is passed only to COMP-009 in memory.

## Rationale

- Option 1 protects against offline flash reading only if the partition key is safe; defense in depth is required by Cybersecurity.
- Option 3 is limited by HSM secure storage capacity (16 slots) and slow write performance.

## Consequences

- Every reconnection needs an HSM unwrap operation (measured: 4–7 ms).
- COMP-003 depends on the HSM being available during startup.

## Open point

The behavior when the HSM is not available or returns an error during startup (e.g. HSM firmware update in progress, HSM self-test failure) is **not defined**. Options discussed: delay reconnection until the HSM is available, or skip automatic reconnection for this ignition cycle. Owner: Karim Haddad.
title: ADR-003 – Encrypted Link-Key Storage with HSM Key Wrapping

text:
# ADR-004 – Delta Synchronization of the Phonebook

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-054 |
| Status | **Accepted** (2026-07-22) |
| Deciders | Ioana Marin, Tobias Kern, Andrei Popescu |

## Context

Downloading the complete phonebook on each connection takes up to several minutes for large phonebooks, creates load on the Bluetooth link during startup, and consumes memory (RSK-07). PBAP 1.2 provides a database identifier and folder version counters that allow a client to detect changes.

## Decision

COMP-007 uses **delta synchronization**:

1. On connection, read the PBAP *database identifier* and the *primary/secondary folder version counters*.
2. If the database identifier is unchanged and the counters are unchanged, keep the local copy – no download.
3. If counters changed, download only the vCard listing with handles and download vCards that are new or changed.
4. If the database identifier changed, or the phone does not support PBAP 1.2 features, fall back to a full download.

Call history is always downloaded completely, because the lists are short.

## Consequences

- Typical reconnection with an unchanged phonebook needs no phonebook transfer.
- COMP-007 must store the database identifier and counters per phone.
- Memory profiling was done with a reference phonebook of 5,000 contacts.

## Not covered

The ADR does not define how many contacts the vehicle stores at most.
title: ADR-004 – Delta Synchronization of the Phonebook

text:
# ADR-005 – Diagnostics Event Schema

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-055 |
| Status | **Accepted** (2026-07-29) |
| Deciders | Elena Rusu, Tobias Kern |

## Context

REQ-006 requires diagnostic events for start, completion, failure and duration of each reconnection attempt. The events are consumed by workshop diagnostics, by test automation (HiL), and potentially by a backend.

## Decision

All events use the following structure:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| eventType | enum | RECONNECT_START, RECONNECT_COMPLETE, RECONNECT_FAIL, RECONNECT_DURATION, PROFILE_FAIL |
| timestamp | uint64 | ms since epoch (UTC) or since boot if time is not synchronized |
| deviceIdHash | bytes[8] | Truncated SHA-256 of BD_ADDR + vehicle salt |
| attemptId | uint16 | Increments per attempt; same for all events of one attempt |
| durationMs | uint32 | Only for RECONNECT_DURATION |
| resultCode | uint8 | PCON result code (PC-048) |
| swVersion | string[16] | Version of COMP-002 |

## Rationale

- Hashing the BD_ADDR avoids storing personal data in the diagnostic buffer.
- `attemptId` allows correlating events with text traces.

## Consequences

- Test automation reads the events via the diagnostic routine (PC-036).
- Any backend upload (still undecided, see PC-036) would use the same fields.

## Not covered

How future changes to this schema are handled (e.g. adding fields while older readers exist) was not part of this decision.
title: ADR-005 – Diagnostics Event Schema

text:
# ADR-006 – Block Inquiry during Startup

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-056 |
| Status | **Accepted** (2026-08-07) |
| Deciders | Andrei Popescu, Tobias Kern |

## Context

During the analysis of DEF-001, traces showed that inquiry (device discovery) started by the HMI device list screen at startup occupied the radio and the request queue of COMP-009 while COMP-002 tried to reconnect the phone.

## Decision

Inquiry is blocked for **20 seconds** after BT_READY (parameter `BT_INQUIRY_BLOCK_S`). Inquiry requests during this time are delayed, not rejected. If the driver explicitly opens the "Add device" screen, the block is lifted immediately.

## Consequences

- The "Add device" screen may need up to a few seconds longer to show devices if opened early – accepted by HMI (Jonas Weber).
- This decision complements, but does not replace, the priority queue (DEF-001 fix).
title: ADR-006 – Block Inquiry during Startup

## Test levels

| Level | Environment | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Unit tests | Developer PC / CI | Logic of individual components |
| Component integration | SiL | Interaction of PCON components with simulated stack and vehicle |
| System tests | HiL | Real head unit, real Bluetooth radio, reference phones |
| Vehicle tests | Prototype vehicles | Real vehicle network, real environment |
| Field tests | Test fleet | Long-term behavior, real usage |

## Principles

- Every approved requirement is verified on at least one level above unit tests.
- Timing requirements (REQ-002) must be verified in HiL **and** Vehicle, because SiL does not reproduce radio timing.
- Defects are reproduced on the lowest level possible.
- All HiL and vehicle executions produce traces in the TraceRepository.

## Evidence for release

The release evidence consists of HiL and vehicle executions for all approved requirements. For requirements that do not depend on radio behavior (e.g. REQ-006 diagnostics, parts of REQ-003), the team discussed whether SiL executions alone could be accepted as verification evidence. Quality Management has not yet confirmed this; currently there is **no agreed rule**.

## Test automation

- SiL: fully automated, nightly.
- HiL: automated with robot-controlled phones (button presses via phone automation frameworks); weekly full regression and on-demand runs.
- Vehicle: manual execution following test procedures; results entered in the TestManagementSystem.

## Roles

Test Lead: Sofia Brandt. HiL: Daniel Szabo. Vehicle: Lukas Becker.

text:
# Performance Measurement Method – Reconnection Time

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-074 |
| Owner | Sofia Brandt |
| Last updated | 2026-08-30 |

## Purpose

This page defines how the reconnection time is measured in HiL and vehicle tests, so that results from different environments and testers are comparable.

## Measurement points

| Point | Definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **t0** | **Ignition ON** – rising edge of KL15 as received by COMP-001 (trace "Vehicle ignition event received.") | COMP-001 trace |
| t1 | Phone shown as connected: COMP-002 state `PROFILE_RESTORE` reached (ACL + HFP SLC) | COMP-002 trace |

**Reconnection time = t1 − t0.**

The measurement starts at ignition because this is what the driver experiences. Using the KL15 trace makes the measurement independent of internal events.

## Procedure (HiL)

1. Phone paired and connected; ignition OFF for at least 60 s.
2. Switch KL15 ON via restbus.
3. Read t0 and t1 from the trace (automated parser `reconn_time.py`).
4. Record the value in the TestManagementSystem with 0.1 s resolution.

## Procedure (Vehicle)

1. Driver enters the vehicle with the phone in the pocket, Bluetooth enabled.
2. Switch on ignition.
3. Trace is captured on the head unit; values extracted after the drive.

## Special cases

- If the head unit reboots during the measurement, the execution is invalid and repeated.
title: Performance Measurement Method – Reconnection Time

text:
# Test Data and Trace Analysis Guide

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-075 |
| Owner | Elena Rusu |
| Last updated | 2026-08-25 |

## Where to find traces

- HiL and vehicle traces: TraceRepository, searchable by execution ID (EXEC-xxx) and trace ID (TRACE-xxx).
- SiL traces: GitLab CI job artifacts, kept for 14 days.

## Reading a reconnection trace

Look for these lines in order:

1. `Vehicle ignition event received.` (COMP-001)
2. `Bluetooth subsystem available; reconnection request submitted.` (COMP-002)
3. Queue wait warnings from COMP-009, e.g. `Reconnection request remained in the connection queue for X seconds.`
4. `Reconnection completed in X seconds` (INFO if ≤ 10 s, WARN/ERROR if > 10 s)
5. Profile messages from COMP-004.

## Typical patterns

| Pattern | Likely cause | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Long gap between 2 and the connect request | Queue wait in COMP-009 | DEF-001 |
| "Device service discovery response was delayed." | Slow SDP response by phone | TRACE-004 |
| Completion missing in diagnostic events but present in text trace | Shutdown race | DEF-002 |
| "Media audio profile restoration failed" | A2DP/HFP race | DEF-003 |

## Correlation

Use the `attemptId` (4 hex digits in the trace line) to correlate text traces with diagnostic events from COMP-005.

## Example: EXEC-010

TRACE-006 (ignition event, 08:45:03) → TRACE-007 (queue wait 8.9 s) → TRACE-008 (reconnected after 18.0 s). Classified as DEF-001.
title: Test Data and Trace Analysis Guide

# Endurance and Soak Testing

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-081 |
| Owner | Daniel Szabo |
| Last updated | 2026-09-05 |

## Goal

Find failures that only appear after many ignition cycles or long uptime: memory leaks, file system growth, stack resource exhaustion, timing drift.

## HiL soak setup

- Bench: HIL-BT-01 (needs transport mode off, normal voltage).
- Phones: RP-01 and RP-07, permanently charged.
- Cycle: KL15 ON → wait for connection → play media 60 s → place automated call 30 s → KL15 OFF → wait 90 s.
- One cycle takes about 4 minutes, so roughly 15 cycles per hour.
- Monitored: RSS of all PCON processes, size of `/persist/bt/`, reconnection time per cycle, error events.

## Pass criteria

- No crash or restart of a PCON process.
- RSS growth less than 1 MB over the whole run.
- No reconnection above 20 s.

## Duration

The run duration for the R1 soak test has not been fixed. Sofia proposed 72 hours, Daniel pointed out that a 72-hour run blocks HIL-BT-01 for three days and conflicts with the Audio team booking.

# Defect Management Process and Severity Definitions

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-083 |
| Owner | Sofia Brandt |

## Severity

| Severity | Definition | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | Requirement with priority Critical violated in normal use, or safety/security impact, no workaround | Reconnection regularly above limit |
| High | Main function impaired, workaround exists | Media audio not restored, manual reconnect helps |
| Medium | Secondary function impaired | Diagnostic event missing |
| Low | Cosmetic or minor | Wrong text in a log line |

## Triage SLA

| Severity | Triage within |
|---|---|
| Critical | 1 working day |
| High | 3 working days |

Triage happens in the defect triage meeting (Tuesday and Thursday) or ad hoc for Critical defects.

## Lifecycle

1. Tester creates a Bug with environment, SW version, execution ID, trace.
2. Triage sets severity and assignee.
3. Developer fixes and links the merge request.
4. **Verification and closure are done by the test team only.** A Bug can only be closed by a tester after the fix has been verified on HiL or in the vehicle in the environment where the defect was found. SiL verification alone is not sufficient for closing.
5. Reopened Bugs return to triage.

## Defect data

Defects are exported as DEF-xxx records to the DefectTrackingSystem export used for the traceability graph. Each defect must be linked to at least one failed execution and one affected component.

text:
# DEF-001 – Delayed Bluetooth Reconnection after Ignition – Analysis

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-084 |
| Defect | DEF-001 |
| Severity | **Critical** |
| Status | Open (fix in review) |
| Created | 2026-07-17 |
| Affected component | COMP-002 Bluetooth Connection Manager |
| Assignee | Radu Ionescu |

## Symptom

Bluetooth reconnection sometimes exceeds the 10-second requirement because the connection request remains queued longer than expected.

## Affected executions

| Execution | Env | Time (s) |
|---|---|---|
| EXEC-003 | SiL | 12.1 |
| EXEC-006 | HiL | 15.4 |
| EXEC-008 | HiL | 13.8 |
| EXEC-010 | Vehicle | 18.0 |
| EXEC-016 | Vehicle | 11.6 |

## Root cause

COMP-009 processed connection-related requests in strict FIFO order. At startup, the queue already contained:

- SDP queries left from the previous session's service discovery,
- an inquiry started by the HMI device list screen,
- PBAP session setup requests for a phone that was not in range.

The reconnection request of COMP-002 was placed behind them. TRACE-007 shows 8.9 s queue wait in EXEC-010.

## Fix

1. COMP-009 2.0.4: priority flag for queue entries.
2. COMP-002 2.3.1: reconnection requests sent with priority `HIGH`.
3. ADR-006: inquiry blocked for 20 s after BT_READY.

## Verification plan

- HiL: TEST-002, TEST-007, TEST-008 with all reference phones.
- Vehicle: TEST-002 and TEST-007 on MER-P03 and MER-P05.

## Severity

The defect violates REQ-002 (priority Critical) in normal use and was observed in every environment. Severity Critical as reported.
title: DEF-001 – Delayed Bluetooth Reconnection after Ignition – Analysis

text:
# DEF-002 – Missing Reconnection Completion Diagnostic Event – Analysis

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-085 |
| Defect | DEF-002 |
| Severity | Medium |
| Status | In Progress |
| Created | 2026-07-22 |
| Affected component | COMP-005 Connectivity Diagnostics Service |
| Assignee | Elena Rusu |

## Symptom

The diagnostic service does not always record the completion event for a successful reconnection attempt. Found in EXEC-012 (Vehicle, TEST-006); trace TRACE-009.

## Root cause

COMP-005 buffers events in memory and writes them to the ring buffer file every 500 ms. When the infotainment system shuts down within about **200 ms** after the completion event (short ignition cycle in the test), COMP-010 confirms the shutdown after its 800 ms deadline while COMP-005 is still waiting for the HSM-backed file write. The completion event is lost.

## Fix

COMP-005 1.2.1: write COMPLETE and FAIL events synchronously; flush on `ShutdownPrepare` with priority.

## Release

Target version 1.2.1. Whether 1.2.1 is part of R1 or R2 is **not decided** (see PC-063).
title: DEF-002 – Missing Reconnection Completion Diagnostic Event – Analysis

text:
# DEF-003 – Media Audio Profile not Restored – Analysis

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-086 |
| Defect | DEF-003 |
| Severity | High |
| Status | Resolved |
| Created | 2026-07-24 |
| Affected component | COMP-004 Bluetooth Profile Service |
| Assignee | Nina Hoffmann |

## Symptom

The phone reconnects successfully but the media audio profile is not restored in some vehicle executions. Found in EXEC-014 (Vehicle, TEST-005), trace TRACE-010.

## Root cause

COMP-004 3.1.0 started the A2DP connection while the HFP service level connection was still being set up. Some phones (RP-03, RP-09) reject the A2DP connection in this situation, and COMP-004 did not retry it.

## Fix

COMP-004 3.1.1 waits for the HFP SLC to be completely established before starting A2DP. The fix was verified in HiL (TEST-005, all reference phones, 3 runs each) and in the vehicle on MER-P05.

## Notes

The startup sequence page (PC-043) was created before this fix.
title: DEF-003 – Media Audio Profile not Restored – Analysis

text:
# Troubleshooting Guide for Testers

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-088 |
| Owner | Sofia Brandt |
| Last updated | 2026-09-10 |

## Phone does not reconnect after ignition

1. Check the status icon: grey = disconnected, animated = still trying.
2. Check that Bluetooth is enabled on the phone and the phone is not connected to another device.
3. Check in the trace whether `BT_READY` was reached.
4. If the trace shows authentication failure (HCI 0x05/0x06), the phone has probably deleted the vehicle. Remove the vehicle on the phone and the phone in the vehicle, then pair again.
5. If the trace shows long queue waits, attach the trace to DEF-001 (if SW < 2.3.1).

## Phone connected but no media audio

- Check the HMI shows "Partially connected".
- On SW with COMP-004 3.1.0, this is DEF-003; update to 3.1.1.
- If the phone is used with CarPlay/Android Auto, A2DP is intentionally not used (REQ-028).

## No contacts

- Check contact sharing permission on the phone.
- Check PhonebookStatus in the trace.

## Reconnection takes long only on one bench

- Check the attenuator setting; after link-loss tests it may still be at a high value.
- Check for other phones in the room (LIM-03).

## Collecting data for a bug

Software version, environment, execution ID, phone model and OS, trace file, diagnostic events (`ReadConnectivityEvents`).
title: Troubleshooting Guide for Testers

# Build and Integration Process

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-090 |
| Owner | Andrei Popescu |
| Last updated | 2026-08-15 |

## Repository

All PCON components live in the GitLab repository **`pcon-connectivity`**, one folder per component under `/components/<component-name>`. Interfaces are in `/interfaces`, configuration in `/config`.

## Pipeline stages

1. **lint** – clang-tidy, cpplint, proto lint.
2. **build** – Yocto SDK cross build for HU4 (aarch64) and native x86-64 build for SiL.
3. **unit** – unit tests with coverage report.
4. **sil-smoke** – 25 SiL scenarios (merge requests) or full suite (nightly at 02:00 CET).
5. **package** – creation of the PCON layer package `pcon-<version>.ipk` set.
6. **publish** – upload to the internal artifact repository.

## Integration into the HU4 image

The HU4 integration team pulls PCON packages weekly (Wednesday) into the platform image. Hotfixes can be requested via the integration channel.

## Versions

Each component has its own semantic version (PC-092); the PCON release (e.g. "Connectivity SW 2.3.0") is the version of COMP-002 by convention.

## Release artifacts

Release builds are produced from `release/r1.x` branches and published with a release tag. The Platform team's handling of the final HU4 image is described in the platform documentation.
title: Build and Integration Process

text:
# Branching and Versioning

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-092 |
| Owner | Andrei Popescu |
| Last updated | 2026-06-30 |

## Branching model

- **Trunk-based development** on `main`.
- Short-lived feature branches `feature/PCON-<id>-<short-name>`, merged within 3 days where possible.
- Release branches `release/r1.x` are created at the B-Sample freeze; fixes are made on `main` first and cherry-picked to the release branch.
- Hotfix branches are not used.

## Versioning

- Each component uses **semantic versioning** (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH).
- MAJOR: incompatible interface change; MINOR: new functionality; PATCH: bug fix.
- Interface changes in `pcon.proto` follow backward-compatible evolution (PC-044).

## Tags

- Release tags: `pcon-r1.<n>` on the release branch.
- Component tags are not used; component versions are maintained in `component.yaml`.
title: Branching and Versioning

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-095 |
| Owner | Karim Haddad |
| Last updated | 2026-07-14 |

## TARA result

A Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment was performed for the Bluetooth interface of HU4. The Bluetooth attack surface is rated **"medium"**.

| Threat | Risk | Measure |
|---|---|---|
| Extraction of link keys from flash | High | HSM key wrapping (ADR-003, REQ-022) |
| Impersonation of a paired phone | Medium | SSP Numeric Comparison only (REQ-021) |
| Connection flooding / DoS | Medium | Reject unpaired devices at stack level (REQ-023) |
| Malformed vCards from phone | Medium | Fuzz testing of COMP-007 parser |
| Personal data leakage via logs | Medium | Hashed device IDs in diagnostic events (ADR-005) |

## Residual topics

- Text traces still contain device names and Bluetooth addresses (see PC-049). Whether pseudonymization is required for traces in production builds is open.
- Startup behavior when the HSM is unavailable is open (see ADR-003).

## Security testing

- Fuzzing of PBAP/vCard parser (weekly, SiL).
- Penetration test of the Bluetooth interface by an external lab, planned for C-Sample.
title: Cybersecurity Concept – Summary for Connectivity

text:
# Functional Safety Classification

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page ID | PC-096 |
| Owner | Tobias Kern |
| Last updated | 2026-06-02 |

## Classification

All PCON functions are classified as **QM** (quality managed, no ASIL) according to the item definition of the infotainment system.

## Rationale

- Phone connectivity does not influence vehicle dynamics or any safety-relevant actuator.
- Emergency calls (eCall) are handled by the telematics unit with its own audio path and are out of scope for PCON.
- Driver distraction is addressed by HMI guidelines (e.g. no popups for failed reconnection, REQ-027), not by functional safety.

## Consequences

- Standard QM development process (ASPICE level 2 target) applies.
- No safety requirements are allocated to PCON components.
title: Functional Safety Classification

**Why only one retry?**
Because a second retry cannot finish within 10 s (page timeout 5.12 s). See ADR-001.

**Why does the secondary phone not play music?**
REQ-010: the secondary phone is connected with HFP only.

**Can I use a phone that is not on the reference list for tests?**
For exploratory tests yes; for release evidence only reference phones count.

**What happens if I enter the car while I am already on a call?**
This scenario was collected in the requirements clarification (PC-059) and is part of the exploratory test charter.

**Where are the traces of a vehicle execution?**
In the TraceRepository, searchable by execution ID.

**Who decides about requirement changes?**
The Product Owner, Mara Lindqvist (PC-004).

**Why are there two different HiL benches?**
HIL-BT-01 supports transport-mode simulation, HIL-BT-02 does not (PC-068).

**How do I get the Sylvan portal access?**
Ask Tobias Kern (PC-097).

text:
## ADR-01 — Modular monolith for initial release
**Corpus page:** 76/100 | **Section:** Architecture decisions / ADR | **Status:** Approved baseline

**Scope.** Status: Accepted for the fictional TeamFlow baseline. The decision governs implementation until replaced by a documented ADR.

### Context and problem

TeamFlow needs many closely related transactions across projects, tasks, sprints and permissions.

### Decision

Deploy one server application with modules for identity, workspace, projects, tasks, planning, notifications and reporting. Cross-module references use explicit internal interfaces.

### Alternative considered

Microservices per domain were considered, but distributed authorization and consistency would exceed first-release operational needs.

### Benefits and rationale

Simplifies shared transactions, local development and cross-domain rule enforcement.

### Costs and trade-offs

Module boundaries can erode unless reviewed; deployment still scales as a unit.

### Verification criteria

No public handler reaches directly into another module’s persistence tables without a designated interface.

### Change control

A proposal to supersede this decision must identify impacted business-rule IDs, changed API contracts, migration implications and the result of the verification check above. This ADR does not permit bypassing tenant isolation, permission checks or required audit events.

*Operational references: BR-01; BR-22; BR-32; GL-07; GL-08.*

## ADR-02 — PostgreSQL as transactional system of record
**Corpus page:** 77/100 | **Section:** Architecture decisions / ADR | **Status:** Approved baseline

**Scope.** Status: Accepted for the fictional TeamFlow baseline. The decision governs implementation until replaced by a documented ADR.

### Context and problem

Tenant-scoped projects, task transitions, membership and sprint constraints require transactional data integrity.

### Decision

Use PostgreSQL to store relational domain records, unique keys, membership grants and audit references. Enforce foreign keys and unique constraints.

### Alternative considered

A document database was considered for flexibility, but would make dependency and membership consistency harder to audit.

### Benefits and rationale

Transactions guard task state checks and writes; relational constraints protect stable keys.

### Costs and trade-offs

High-volume full-text workloads need a separate index and deliberate refresh strategy.

### Verification criteria

Tests attempt concurrent creation of the same project key, conflicting sprint activations and cyclic dependency links.

### Change control

A proposal to supersede this decision must identify impacted business-rule IDs, changed API contracts, migration implications and the result of the verification check above. This ADR does not permit bypassing tenant isolation, permission checks or required audit events.

*Operational references: BR-01; BR-22; BR-32; GL-07; GL-08.*

## ADR-03 — Tenant separation through workspace IDs
**Corpus page:** 78/100 | **Section:** Architecture decisions / ADR | **Status:** Approved baseline

**Scope.** Status: Accepted for the fictional TeamFlow baseline. The decision governs implementation until replaced by a documented ADR.

### Context and problem

An account may work in multiple organizations while every API and background job must honor tenant boundaries.

### Decision

Each domain row includes workspace_id; repository calls require trusted workspace context and access policies; exports recheck scope.

### Alternative considered

Database-per-tenant was considered but rejected for first-release administration and migration complexity.

### Benefits and rationale

Consistent scoping applies to REST endpoints, report generation, search and file access.

### Costs and trade-offs

Missed scoping can cause severe leakage; code review and automated isolation tests are mandatory.

### Verification criteria

Cross-tenant object ID probes always return nonrevealing responses, including for search facets and downloadable files.

### Change control

A proposal to supersede this decision must identify impacted business-rule IDs, changed API contracts, migration implications and the result of the verification check above. This ADR does not permit bypassing tenant isolation, permission checks or required audit events.

## ADR-04 — Event-driven notifications and webhooks
**Corpus page:** 79/100 | **Section:** Architecture decisions / ADR | **Status:** Approved baseline

**Scope.** Status: Accepted for the fictional TeamFlow baseline. The decision governs implementation until replaced by a documented ADR.

### Context and problem

Task mutations must not block on email services or third-party webhook availability.

### Decision

Write an outbox event with a successful domain transaction, then process notifications and webhooks asynchronously via retryable workers.

### Alternative considered

Synchronous HTTP calls inside task transactions were rejected because remote failures would make local tasks unreliable.

### Benefits and rationale

External failures cannot roll back successful updates; event IDs support deduplication.

### Costs and trade-offs

Delivery is eventually consistent, requiring visible retry status and safe dead-letter handling.

### Verification criteria

Duplicate event delivery causes no duplicate in-app notifications or other internal side effects.

### Change control

A proposal to supersede this decision must identify impacted business-rule IDs, changed API contracts, migration implications and the result of the verification check above. This ADR does not permit bypassing tenant isolation, permission checks or required audit events.

*Operational references: BR-01; BR-22; BR-32; GL-07; GL-08.*

## ADR-05 — Short-lived access tokens and rotating sessions
**Corpus page:** 80/100 | **Section:** Architecture decisions / ADR | **Status:** Approved baseline

**Scope.** Status: Accepted for the fictional TeamFlow baseline. The decision governs implementation until replaced by a documented ADR.

### Context and problem

The browser client needs secure access to workspace APIs with immediate revocation when membership or session security changes.

### Decision

Issue short-lived access tokens with a server-backed session and refresh-token rotation; all API handlers perform current authorization.

Long-lived bearer tokens without session state were rejected because revocation would lag.

Sessions can be revoked and token compromise detected through refresh reuse.

### Costs and trade-offs

Interactive user experience needs token refresh handling and session cleanup.

Login lockout, logout, refresh reuse and role revocation have integration tests.

## ADR-06 — Object storage with quarantine scanning
**Corpus page:** 81/100 | **Section:** Architecture decisions / ADR | **Status:** Approved baseline

**Scope.** Status: Accepted for the fictional TeamFlow baseline. The decision governs implementation until replaced by a documented ADR.

### Context and problem

Attachments may contain untrusted binary data and task visibility can change after upload.

### Decision

Keep file bytes in private object storage; scan before release; issue time-limited download URLs after server-side authorization.

### Alternative considered

Storing blobs directly in the primary relational database was rejected to simplify capacity and virus-scanning workflows.

Preserves task database performance and supports separate file retention controls.

Object lifecycle reconciliation must clean up abandoned quarantined uploads.

**Corpus page:** 85/100 | **Section:** Architecture decisions / ADR | **Status:** Approved baseline

**Scope.** Status: Accepted for the fictional TeamFlow baseline. The decision governs implementation until replaced by a documented ADR.

### Context and problem

Accidental deletion, database failure and file-store incidents must not silently invalidate active projects.

Create encrypted daily database backups and keep them for 30 days; object metadata recovery is checked with periodic restore rehearsals.

Provides a documented disaster-recovery path and auditable rehearsal evidence.

## API-01 — Authentication and credentials
**Corpus page:** 61/100 | **Section:** API contracts / Integration specs | **Status:** Approved baseline

**Scope.** Versioned access-token and session endpoints. Endpoints below use /v1, JSON payloads, authenticated principals where stated and resource IDs that are opaque strings.

### Endpoint 1: POST /v1/auth/register

**Authorization: Public**

`Request:  {"email":"dev@example.test","password":"<secret>"}`

`Success:  201 {"user_id":"usr_74","email_verified":false}`

Errors: 400 INVALID_EMAIL; 409 EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED.

### Endpoint 2: POST /v1/auth/login

**Authorization: Verified account**

`Request:  {"email":"dev@example.test","password":"<secret>"}`

`Success:  200 {"access_token":"<redacted>","session_id":"ses_9","expires_in":900}`

Errors: 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS; 423 ACCOUNT_LOCKED.

### Contract invariants

Refresh tokens are delivered using a secure channel, rotated on use and never logged. POST /v1/auth/logout revokes the current session and is safe to repeat. Date-time values are UTC.

- All errors use {"error":{"code":"UPPER_SNAKE_CASE","message":"...","correlation_id":"..."}}. Authorization is evaluated using current workspace and project grants.

- Client-supplied resource IDs never bypass tenant scoping. All timestamps are UTC ISO 8601; date-only values follow the project time zone.

*Related policy and flows: BR-02; BR-03; FS-01; FS-02; ADR-05.*

## BR-01 — Workspace isolation
**Corpus page:** 1/100 | **Section:** Business rules / Product requirements | **Status:** Approved baseline

**Scope.** Policy intent: Workspaces are the top-level security and ownership boundary.

### Normative business rules

- **BR-01-R01.** A workspace has a unique immutable ID, name of 3-80 characters, billing owner and creation timestamp.

- **BR-01-R02.** Every project, task, sprint, file, invitation and notification belongs to exactly one workspace.

- **BR-01-R03.** A user may belong to multiple workspaces, but data from one workspace is never included in another workspace query.

- **BR-01-R04.** Creating a workspace gives its creator the Workspace Owner role in that workspace.

A contributor submits code for review and moves a task from IN_PROGRESS to IN_REVIEW; a reviewer requests changes by returning it to IN_PROGRESS.

**Corpus page:** 12/100 | **Section:** Business rules / Product requirements | **Status:** Approved baseline

**Scope.** Policy intent: Planning fields are independent from state transitions.

- **BR-12-R03.** Estimates are stored as positive integer minutes and may be changed until a task becomes DONE.

- **BR-12-R05.** An estimate adjustment does not change previously logged actual time.

- **BR-12-R06.** Overdue status is derived from the project time zone and must not be stored as a separately editable task state.

A task due on 2026-11-12 is overdue after that calendar date in the project time zone if it is not DONE.

### Boundary and rejection example

A negative estimate or malformed date fails validation and leaves the saved plan unchanged.

## BR-33 — Imports and external migrations
**Corpus page:** 33/100 | **Section:** Business rules / Product requirements | **Status:** Approved baseline

**Scope.** Policy intent: Structured imports are validated before they create objects.

### Normative business rules

- **BR-33-R01.** Workspace ADMINs may import projects from a versioned CSV or JSON bundle.

- **BR-33-R02.** Import previews identify invalid task keys, unknown assignees, invalid statuses and broken dependencies.

- **BR-33-R03.** An import does not publish partial data if mandatory validation fails; the caller receives a validation report.

- **BR-33-R04.** Original external identifiers are kept in an optional import_reference field for traceability.

- **BR-33-R05.** Imported task states must map to an allowed TeamFlow state; unmapped states are not silently coerced.

**Scope.** Troubleshooting answers describe observable TeamFlow behavior for support and engineering teams. Source references are provided with each answer for verification.

Verification creates an account, not workspace or project membership. Accept an invitation and ask a project manager for the project grant.

Invitations are single-use and expire after seven calendar days; an admin must issue a fresh one.

Project membership may have been removed; the server checks current authorization on every read and mutation.

No. Another OWNER must already exist before the last owner role may be removed.

*References: BR-04.*

Five consecutive incorrect password attempts trigger a fifteen-minute lockout. Reset or wait according to account policy.

*References: BR-03; FS-02.*

## GL-01 — Naming, IDs and schema conventions
**Corpus page:** 86/100 | **Section:** Guidelines / Conventions | **Status:** Approved baseline

**Scope.** Engineering conventions apply to TeamFlow services, clients, documentation and integration tests. Conventions do not replace normative business rules.

### Required engineering conventions

- **GL-01-R01.** Resource IDs are opaque prefixes: ws_, usr_, prj_, task_, spr_, com_, att_, ntf_ and job_.

- **GL-01-R02.** Human-facing task keys use PROJECTKEY-NNNN and remain immutable after creation.

- **GL-01-R03.** Database field and API JSON keys use snake_case; domain enums use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE.

- **GL-01-R04.** Plural REST resource names represent collections; verbs appear only on explicit transition actions.

- **GL-01-R05.** Each schema change has a migration and rollback strategy; never reuse a retired enum code.

- **GL-01-R06.** Document headings carry stable BR, FS, API, ADR or GL IDs and do not depend on pagination.

### Concrete example

Example valid task key: MOB-0042; valid JSON: {"assignee_id":"usr_74","state":"IN_REVIEW"}.

### Review and test criterion

CI checks schema examples and IDs for uniqueness.

### Documentation practice

Use exact source IDs when discussing requirement changes. If two approved sources disagree, preserve their statements until a product decision is recorded; do not silently treat an example, API response or an undocumented assumption as an overriding policy.

# Reservation approval — Architecture decision

Document ID: `TN-APR-ADR`  
Owner: Matei Ionescu, Tech Lead  
Status: Active  
Applies to: ToolNest 1.1  
Published: 2026-08-28T08:00:00Z

## Context

High-value equipment uses a staff approval gate. An approval belongs to a specific request version; it is neither a standing privilege for a borrower nor permission to ignore an availability conflict.

## Requirements and guidance

### TN-APR-ADR-01

Approvals are versioned decisions stored with the reservation, not mutable boolean fields on user accounts.

### TN-APR-ADR-02

A transaction releases the interval at the same time that rejection becomes visible.

### TN-APR-ADR-03

The expiry worker uses server time and a compare-and-set transition so a completed approval cannot also expire.

Document ID: `TN-INT-ADR`  
Owner: Matei Ionescu, Tech Lead  
Status: Active

Published: 2026-08-28T08:00:00Z

## Context

A course scheduler integrates with ToolNest through a versioned REST API and event subscriptions. Integrations receive lab-scoped service credentials and must tolerate retries, duplicate webhook deliveries, and stale updates.

## Requirements and guidance

### TN-INT-ADR-01

The public integration API uses the /v1 prefix; internal database tables are not an integration contract.

### TN-INT-ADR-02

Domain events are published from an outbox after the corresponding database transaction commits.

### TN-INT-ADR-03

Idempotency scope includes authenticated actor and route so two different integrations cannot read each other's stored responses by choosing the same key.
title: External API and webhook delivery — Architecture decision

passages.text: Webhook requests include X-ToolNest-Event-Id, X-ToolNest-Timestamp, and X-ToolNest-Signature headers.
A versioned mutation with a stale If-Match returns 412 VERSION_MISMATCH rather than overwriting a newer resource.
A successful idempotent retry within the retention window returns the original response status and body.
Revoking a service credential rejects subsequent requests using that credential without waiting for an application restart.

# Reservation intervals and availability — Architecture decision

Document ID: `TN-RSV-ADR`  
Owner: Matei Ionescu, Tech Lead  
Status: Active  
Applies to: ToolNest 1.1  
Published: 2026-08-28T08:00:00Z

## Context

Borrowers reserve a physical unit for a bounded interval. Availability is computed from committed reservations and operational blocks, so the calendar and the create endpoint must agree when two people compete for the same unit.

## Requirements and guidance

### TN-RSV-ADR-01

PostgreSQL exclusion constraints protect unit intervals from concurrent overlapping writes.

### TN-RSV-ADR-02

The application expands no implicit cleaning buffer around an ordinary reservation.

### TN-RSV-ADR-03

A reservation owns one assigned unit; substitution is an explicit operation rather than a change to the model name.
title: Reservation intervals and availability — Architecture decision

passages.text: POST /v1/reservations requires assetId, startAt, endAt, and purpose; an overlap returns 409 RESERVATION_CONFLICT.

Reservation conflicts are enforced inside the same database transaction that creates the reservation.

Offer ranking uses stored joinedAt, not email delivery order.

Waiting-list entries are scoped to an equipment model, pickup lab, and requested interval.

### TN-WAI-BR-02

Eligible entries for the same freed interval are considered in order of joinedAt, with entry UUID as the tie-breaker.

### TN-WAI-BR-03

A waiting-list offer temporarily blocks the offered unit until acceptance or offer expiry.

### TN-WAI-BR-04

A borrower may have only one active waiting-list entry for the same model, lab, and interval.

### TN-WAI-BR-05

A waiting-list offer expires 20 minutes after it is created.
